context: The undirected graph has 9 vertices numbered 0 through 8 in a three-by-three grid. The rows, from top to bottom, are (0, 1, 2), (3, 4, 5), and (6, 7, 8). The graph has 12 undirected edges, all between horizontal or vertical neighbors. There are no diagonal edges. The adjacency table lists the neighbors of each vertex.

frames.announcement: Enqueue the start vertex, 0, and mark it as discovered to begin the traversal.
frames.explanation: In the process diagram, res records vertices removed from the queue. The queue que holds vertices waiting to be processed, shown from front to back. The set visited contains all discovered vertices. Each vertex enters visited as soon as it is enqueued, so even a vertex still waiting in the queue cannot be enqueued twice. Blank slots on the left of the queue are positions vacated by dequeued vertices, not empty elements. Neither the horizontal layout of visited nor the braces below imply any ordering within the set. Initially, enqueue 0 and mark it as discovered: res=[], que=[0], visited={0}. No vertex has been dequeued.
frames.key_state: The queue holds only the start vertex, 0. The discovered set is {0}, and the result is empty.
frames.title: Initialize the queue and set

frames.announcement: Dequeue vertex 0. Enqueue new neighbors 1 and 3.
frames.explanation: Remove vertex 0 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Check the neighbors of 0, vertices 1 and 3. Both are new. Add them in order to the back of que and to visited. The result is res=[0]. The pending queue is que=[1, 3]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 0. Queue from front to back: [1, 3]. Result: [0].
frames.title: Process vertex 0

frames.announcement: Dequeue vertex 1. Enqueue new neighbors 2 and 4.
frames.explanation: Remove vertex 1 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Check the neighbors of 1 in order: 0, 2, 4. Skip 0 because it is in visited. Enqueue 2 and 4 in order and add them to visited. The result is res=[0, 1]. The pending queue is que=[3, 2, 4]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 1. Queue from front to back: [3, 2, 4]. Result: [0, 1].
frames.title: Process vertex 1

frames.explanation: Remove vertex 3 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Check the neighbors of 3 in order: 0, 4, 6. Skip 0 and 4 because they are in visited. Enqueue only 6 and add it to visited. Vertex 1 discovered and enqueued 4 in the previous step. Although 4 is still waiting in the queue, it is never enqueued a second time. The result is res=[0, 1, 3]. The pending queue is que=[2, 4, 6]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 3. Queue from front to back: [2, 4, 6]. Result: [0, 1, 3].
frames.title: Process vertex 3

frames.explanation: Remove vertex 2 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Of the neighbors of 2, vertices 1 and 5, skip 1 because it is in visited. Enqueue 5 and add it to visited. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2]. The pending queue is que=[4, 6, 5]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 2. Queue from front to back: [4, 6, 5]. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2].
frames.title: Process vertex 2

frames.explanation: Remove vertex 4 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Check the neighbors of 4 in order: 1, 3, 5, 7. Skip 1, 3, and 5 because they are in visited. Enqueue 7 and add it to visited. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4]. The pending queue is que=[6, 5, 7]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 4. Queue from front to back: [6, 5, 7]. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2, 4].
frames.title: Process vertex 4

frames.announcement: Dequeue vertex 6. All its neighbors have already been discovered, so no vertex is enqueued.
frames.explanation: Remove vertex 6 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Both neighbors of 6, vertices 3 and 7, are in visited. Vertex 4 discovered and enqueued 7 in the previous step. No new neighbor is enqueued. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6]. The pending queue is que=[5, 7]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 6. Queue from front to back: [5, 7]. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6].
frames.title: Process vertex 6

frames.explanation: Remove vertex 5 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Check the neighbors of 5 in order: 2, 4, 8. Skip 2 and 4 because they are in visited. Enqueue the last new neighbor, 8, and add it to visited. All nine vertices have now been discovered, but 7 and 8 are still in the queue awaiting processing. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5]. The pending queue is que=[7, 8]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 5. Queue from front to back: [7, 8]. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5].
frames.title: Process vertex 5

frames.announcement: Dequeue vertex 7. All its neighbors have already been discovered, so no vertex is enqueued.
frames.explanation: Remove vertex 7 from the front of the queue and append it to res. All three neighbors of 7, vertices 4, 6, and 8, are in visited. No new neighbor is enqueued, and only 8 remains in the queue. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7]. The pending queue is que=[8]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 7. Queue from front to back: [8]. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7].
frames.title: Process vertex 7

frames.announcement: Dequeue vertex 8. All its neighbors have already been discovered, so no vertex is enqueued.
frames.explanation: Remove vertex 8 from the front of the queue and append it to res. Both neighbors of 8, vertices 5 and 7, are in visited. No new neighbor is enqueued, and que is now empty. The result is res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8]. The pending queue is que=[]. The discovered set is visited={0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8}.
frames.key_state: Processed vertex 8. Queue from front to back: []. Result: [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8].
frames.title: Process vertex 8

frames.announcement: With the queue empty, finish the traversal and return the result.
frames.explanation: The queue is empty, que=[]. The loop ends and returns res=[0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8]. The set visited contains all vertices from 0 through 8.
frames.title: Return the traversal result

frames.announcement: The visit order runs from the vertices nearest to 0 to those farthest away.
frames.explanation: This figure summarizes the visit order and omits the queue and the visited set. Dashed blue arrows show the order of visits. For example, 1→3 and 6→5 do not correspond to edges in the original graph. Dashed gray curves separate the distance layers. The table lists the vertices in each layer. The complete visit sequence is [0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 8].
frames.key_state: Starting at 0, visit the distance layers in order: {0}, {1, 3}, {2, 4, 6}, {5, 7}, {8}.
frames.title: Breadth-first traversal overview

result: The order within a distance layer depends on the order in which neighbors are checked, so several breadth-first traversal sequences are possible.
summary: Starting at vertex 0 in the upper left, visit vertices one layer at a time in order of their distance from the start, measured by the fewest edges needed to reach them.

title: Breadth-first traversal of a graph
